quotes.text: He giveth snow like wool: he scattereth the hoarfrost like ashes.
quotes.author: the King James Bible

quotes.text: Hast thou entered into the treasures of the snow? or hast thou seen the treasures of the hail
quotes.author: the King James Bible

quotes.text: The wind goeth toward the south, and turneth about unto the north; it whirleth about continually, and the wind returneth again according to his circuits.
quotes.author: the King James Bible

quotes.text: To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven:
quotes.author: the King James Bible

quotes.text: He that observeth the wind shall not sow; and he that regardeth the clouds shall not reap.
quotes.author: the King James Bible

quotes.text: For, lo, the winter is past, the rain is over and gone; The flowers appear on the earth; the time of the singing of birds is come, and the voice of the turtle is heard in our land;
quotes.author: the King James Bible

quotes.text: When it is evening, ye say, It will be fair weather: for the sky is red.
quotes.author: the King James Bible

quotes.text: And in the morning, It will be foul weather to day: for the sky is red and lowering.
quotes.author: the King James Bible

quotes.text: While the earth remaineth, seedtime and harvest, and cold and heat, and summer and winter, and day and night shall not cease.
quotes.author: the King James Bible

quotes.text: The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament sheweth his handywork.
quotes.author: the King James Bible

quotes.text: Blow, winds, and crack your cheeks! Rage! blow! You cataracts and hurricanoes, spout Till you have drench'd our steeples, drown'd the cocks!
quotes.author: Shakespeare

quotes.text: When that I was and a little tiny boy, With hey, ho, the wind and the rain, A foolish thing was but a toy, For the rain it raineth every day.
quotes.author: Shakespeare

quotes.text: When icicles hang by the wall, And Dick the shepherd blows his nail, And Tom bears logs into the hall, And milk comes frozen home in pail,
quotes.author: Shakespeare

quotes.text: But look, the morn in russet mantle clad, Walks o'er the dew of yon high eastward hill.
quotes.author: Shakespeare

quotes.text: Night's candles are burnt out, and jocund day Stands tiptoe on the misty mountain tops.
quotes.author: Shakespeare

quotes.text: So foul and fair a day I have not seen.
quotes.author: Shakespeare

quotes.text: Fair is foul, and foul is fair: Hover through the fog and filthy air.
quotes.author: Shakespeare

quotes.text: Shall I compare thee to a summer's day? Thou art more lovely and more temperate: Rough winds do shake the darling buds of May,
quotes.author: Shakespeare

quotes.text: That time of year thou mayst in me behold, When yellow leaves, or none, or few do hang Upon those boughs which shake against the cold, Bare ruined choirs, where late the sweet birds sang.
quotes.author: Shakespeare

quotes.text: We are such stuff As dreams are made on, and our little life Is rounded with a sleep.
quotes.author: Shakespeare

quotes.text: WHEN that Aprilis, with his showers swoot The drought of March hath pierced to the root,
quotes.author: Geoffrey Chaucer
quotes.work: The Canterbury Tales, General Prologue (c. 1400; modernised spelling)

quotes.text: Mais où sont les neiges d'antan!
quotes.author: François Villon
quotes.work: Ballade des dames du temps jadis (1461): "But where are the snows of yesteryear?" (Rossetti's English, 1870)

quotes.text: Avoid the month Lenaeon, wretched days, all of them fit to skin an ox, and the frosts which are cruel when Boreas blows over the earth.
quotes.author: Hesiod
quotes.work: Works and Days (c. 700 BC; tr. Evelyn-White, 1914)

quotes.text: So too, after rain, Sunshine and open skies thou mayst forecast, And learn by tokens sure, for then nor dimmed Appear the stars' keen edges, nor the moon As borrowing of her brother's beams to rise, Nor fleecy films to float along the sky.
quotes.author: Virgil
quotes.work: Georgics, book I (29 BC; tr. Rhoades, 1881)

quotes.text: When first the moon recalls her rallying fires, If dark the air clipped by her crescent dim, For folks afield and on the open sea A mighty rain is brewing;
quotes.author: Virgil

quotes.text: Then the crow With full voice, good-for-naught, inviting rain, Stalks on the dry sand mateless and alone.
quotes.author: Virgil

quotes.text: Oft, too, the ant from out her inmost cells, Fretting the narrow path, her eggs conveys;
quotes.author: Virgil

quotes.text: Upon the sun's own face strange colours stray; Dark tells of rain, of east winds fiery-red;
quotes.author: Virgil

quotes.text: But when from regions of the furious North It lightens, and when thunder fills the halls Of Eurus and of Zephyr, all the fields With brimming dikes are flooded, and at sea No mariner but furls his dripping sails.
quotes.author: Virgil

quotes.text: Then to set Snares for the crane, and meshes for the stag, And hunt the long-eared hares, then pierce the doe With whirl of hempen-thonged Balearic sling, While snow lies deep, and streams are drifting ice.
quotes.author: Virgil
